checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: An exchange trade must reach millions of client UIs in ~200ms.

options.label: Clients poll for quotes
options.verdict: A million clients polling once a second is a million requests per second for data that mostly has not changed, and it still lags by up to a second. You pay full price for staleness.

options.label: Push over persistent connections
options.sub: fan out through a pub/sub tier
options.verdict: The exchange feed arrives once and is fanned out to subscribers. Cost tracks actual price changes rather than client count, and the latency budget becomes achievable.

defend.prompt: What does the push tier have to solve?

options.label: Fan-out to millions of concurrent sockets
Guaranteeing every tick reaches every client

defend.explain: Delivering every tick is neither possible nor wanted — a symbol can move faster than a screen refreshes. You send the latest value, coalescing intermediate ticks, and resync on reconnect.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Market open, with price fanout under ~200ms p95.

rungs.note: Which is why load shedding is designed in rather than improvised.
A price a moment stale is tolerable; a wrong balance is not.

checkpoints.explain: Two subsystems with opposite requirements sharing one product: a soft-real-time broadcast path and a strictly consistent transactional one.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.explain: The feed is normalised once, distributed through Kafka, and fanned out to socket gateways holding client connections. Order Service and the ledger are the transactional path — deliberately separate, because they must not be slowed by broadcast load or vice versa.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: At market open, prices freeze for 30 seconds. Orders still execute correctly.
checkpoints.explain: Orders are unaffected, which confirms the transactional path is healthy and the fault is confined to broadcast. The fanout topic is 8M messages behind: at market open every symbol ticks at once, and the consumers cannot drain it. The fix is coalescing — collapse per-symbol updates so you publish the latest price rather than every intermediate tick.

wrong.WebSocket Gateway: More connections than usual, but it is delivering what it receives.
wrong.Feed Handler: 4ms — it is ingesting the exchange feed without difficulty.
wrong.Order Service: Untouched, and that is the clue: the two paths are properly isolated.
